Subject: Faraday Health — multi-account SLA carveout / expedited timeline

Alex / team — quick context and ask. Faraday's procurement flagged a requirement in the SOW for tenant-level SLA guarantees and cross-account telemetry exports (they run multiple internal orgs under one contract). They've made redlines contingent on us delivering: 1) a per-account latency SLO pinning option and 2) an exportable audit stream per tenant for 90 days.

Attachments: Faraday_SOW_v1.pdf, sla_matrix.xlsx (procurement comments highlighted).

Why this is urgent: FH are in final legal review and have said the deal close (~$1.1M ARR) depends on explicit wording + an implementation window. Monica and Alex asked for an honest engineering ETA so they can avoid stalling procurement.

Ask to Product/Eng: can we scope a narrow carveout (config-driven tenant SLO pin + an export hook) that can be delivered as an expedite in the next roadmap cycle? If we can commit to something small and safe (and list tradeoffs) I can move procurement from redlines to signatures.

Proposed immediate steps:
- Product: confirm feasible approach (config vs infra change)
- Eng: ballpark effort and any blocking work (telemetry infra, gating)
- CS/Sales: I'll coordinate the customer expectations and draft the mutual action plan once we have ETA.

Deal details: FH-2026-1197, Region: US.

Thanks — Chlo

On Tue, Sep 1, 2026 at 9:12 AM chloe_martin@redwood.com wrote:
> Alex / team — quick context and ask. Faraday's procurement flagged a requirement in the SOW for tenant-level SLA guarantees and cross-account telemetry exports...

Thanks for the context, Chlo. High-level reaction from Product: conceptually fine as a product-facing toggle+export, but we need to lock the exact guarantees and safety nets. Two immediate questions:

1) Pinning SLOs per tenant — do they require hard isolation (dedicated capacity) or a configuration-level SLA commitment (routing/priority lanes + observability)?
2) Export format — vendor expects a daily signed export (CSV/Parquet) with trace ids and latency buckets? Any PII concerns?

Tradeoffs to call out:
- Hard isolation (dedicated GPUs per tenant) is expensive and will require sales to sign a capacity premium.
- Config-only approach (priority lanes + routing policy) is cheaper but not strict isolation; we'll need fallback policies to preserve other customers' SLAs.

I can slot a short scoping session with Eng to create an 8/20 roadmap ask if we confirm: (A) acceptance criteria, (B) minimal data schema for export, (C) rollout plan for canary + monitoring.

Ben / Jordan — can you weigh in on technical feasibility and rough estimate? I want a two-option plan (fast shim vs full isolation) we can present to Fahady.

-Marissa

On Tue, Sep 1, 2026 at 11:03 AM marissa_cole@redwood.com wrote:
> Thanks for the context, Chlo. High-level reaction from Product: conceptually fine as a product-facing toggle+export...

Quick tech take and constraints:
- Fast shim (option A): add a routing policy that tags requests by tenant and applies a priority queue + KV-prefetch cache pinning. This gives an operational SLO most customers would accept. Work estimate: 2 backend engineers, 3 weeks to prototype + 1 week canary + 1 week to harden docs/tests — ~5 weeks total (assuming no infra blockers).
- Full isolation (option B): per-tenant dedicated pools + deterministic latency guarantees requires infra provisioning changes and capacity accounting. Estimate: 3-4 sprints and a committed reserved capacity model (sales needs to agree to premium).

Telemetry export: we can build a per-tenant export pipeline to s3/parquet; that is straightforward but we need a schema and retention config. No PII in the requested fields other than userid hashes — still require privacy review. Effort: 1 engineer, 2 weeks for initial export + data governance check.

Risks / blockers:
- Storage & egress costs for daily exports (budget/chargeback)
- QA around pressure scenarios (we must ensure priority lanes don't starve public pool)

If Product is comfortable with a shim-first approach we can commit to the 5-week delivery as an expedite (sprint insertion, dedicated engineer time). Otherwise, full isolation will take longer and needs commercial sign-off.

Referencing a short tech note I sketched: tech_shim_note.pdf

-Ben

Thanks all — customer-facing note. Alex/Procurement, appreciate the patience. We're aligned on two options:

A) Shim-first (preferred by Redwood): routing priority + pinned caching for tenant X, with a documented SLO we can guarantee operationally. Delivery ETA: ~5 weeks.
B) Full isolation: dedicated pool and hard isolation with premium pricing; delivery ETA: 3+ sprints and requires reserved capacity agreement.

Monica's suggested mutual action plan (draft):
- Week 0: Redwood confirms option and internal ETA (this thread).
- Week 1: Procurement reviews friction items; sign SOW addendum for expedited lane (if shim) or premium (if isolation).
- Weeks 2–6: Eng implements shim, CS performs canary with non-production traffic.
- Week 7: Production roll & 90-day telemetry export enabled.

We will ask Faraday to accept a documented operational SLO (examples attached in sla_matrix.xlsx) while we deliver the shim; if they need full capacity guarantees, we will add a premium line item to the SOW.

Alex — can you commit to the sign-off timeline above if we lock the 5-week path? Also need a named technical contact for rollout (who on your side will own canary verification?).

-Monica

Thanks team — summary and ask:

Decision: go with the shim-first expedited path (option A) and commit to the 5-week ETA from Ben, with the following constraints:
- Product to publish acceptance criteria and rollback policy by EOD Fri (Marissa).
- Eng to allocate the two engineers and start sprint insertion next Monday; notify infra if any capacity will be reserved for the canary (Ben).
- CS/Sales to update SOW addendum with language binding the operational SLO and the export cadence; procurement to get a signed addendum from Faraday in 7 business days (Monica / Alex).

Commercial note: if Faraday insists on full isolation we will require a reserved capacity commitment and a pricing uplift; otherwise the shim will be covered under standard commercial terms. Closing the deal this quarter is material — FH-2026-1197 is forecasted in Q4 ARR planning.

Please reply-all with a quick acknowledgement and let me know if any team cannot meet their commitments. If we have a green light, I'll push the mutual action plan into HubSpot and schedule a kickoff with Faraday.

-Chloe
